The complete native 0x70-byte layout retains the scale pair at +0x60 and scroll pair at +0x68, constructor, destructor, tween, scale setter and descriptor initializer. The live content context subtracts both actual scroll coordinates.

The live 0x60-byte base retains the original stored layout and pointer-return entry lookup. Native frame position +0x40, frame size +0x48, draw depth +0x54, open tick +0x5C and close tick +0x22 feed the exact context setup.

The complete geometry layout maps to the live 0x4C-byte context with inner height +0x1C, color +0x34, depth +0x38 and clip bounds through +0x48. Original drawing operations remain live. Historical raw free and init declarations map to the native destructor and constructor at 0x8024EE44 and 0x8024EE98. The content alias maps to its actual addition owner at 0x80244364.

The complete added unit has native item-list construction, rendering, tick and destruction. Rendering acquires the scrolled context, draws the frame and stock entries and highlight, retains capacity 0x1E and optional status and scroll bar, and uses the inherited +0x68 scroll coordinate.

The choice renderer at 0x80268C80 acquires the real scrolled context and passes it to the typed selection bar, keeping status and scroll draw order. Other historical entry setup and input changes remain scoped.
Quest Board render uses its real raw-entry receiver with typed default context setup. Historical page and lifetime edits remain outside this audit.
The single historical hunk changes a path-derived guard. The live header retains both text functions and the C setter, now accurately typed to the shared context.
The only substantive historical declaration edit types the first selection bar argument. The active header forwards this actual native type and preserves the existing card and trade interfaces.
Message rendering uses the typed default context. The authored buffer and lifetime portions remain outside this audit.

Shared context storage and the C setter use the native pointer. Both glyph renderers use the real 0x20-byte quad and native clipping and transformation. The existing canonical signed glyph working value and gauge entry linkage differ from the historical unit, so the whole row is left scoped.

Explicit setup uses the original geometry, independent animation and clipping flags, full-screen bounds override, opening-tick subtraction of 7.5 and closing stretch. The default uses the original scale pair. Selection retains three textured quads and the active texture choice. Remaining card initializer and drawer changes stay scoped.
Menu rendering uses the actual context and selection provider. Earlier menu initialization remains in the prerequisite. This mixed historical row stays scoped.
